answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake in a kernel contract before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled task fails independent verification. The contract caps one agent’s voting weight by its locked stake, so minting thousands of names does not multiply influence; the attacker must instead acquire and immobilize real capital across those identities, while risking it on detectable fraud. A sable test task on an isolated island of validators can expose copied answers without granting the claimant reputation.
